blocks.prompt: 16 (a) Using a cryptographic system, a password is generated with 8 characters. Each character can either be a lowercase letter (a-f) or a digit (0-5). How many passwords can be generated if each password must contain exactly 5 lowercase letters and 3 digits? (a) With repetition allowed
blocks.explanation:
A password is ordered. There are 6 letters (a-f) and 6 digits (0-5). Three jobs: choose which 5 of the 8 positions hold letters, fill the letter positions, fill the digit positions.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{5} \times 6^{5} \times 6^{3}\).
steps:
Given: 8 positions; exactly 5 letters from \(\{a, \dots, f\}\) and 3 digits from \(\{0, \dots, 5\}\); repetition allowed.
To find: the number of passwords.
Method: Fundamental principle of counting over the three jobs.

Choose the letter positions
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = {}^{8}C_{3} = 56\]
Why: Choosing positions 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 for letters is one choice whatever order we name them in, so it is a combination; the other 3 positions get digits.

Fill the positions
\[\text{letters: } 6^{5} = 7776\]
\[\text{digits: } 6^{3} = 216\]
Why: With repetition, every letter position has 6 choices and every digit position has 6 choices.

Multiply
\[7776 \times 216 = 1679616\]
\[56 \times 1679616 = 94058496\]
Why: The three jobs are done together. (\(7776 \times 216 = 6^{8}\).)

Check
\[56 \times 6^{8} = 56 \times 1679616\]
\[= 83980800 + 10077696 = 94058496 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(56 = 50 + 6\); multiplying each part and adding gives the same total.

blocks.prompt: 16 (b) Using a cryptographic system, a password is generated with 8 characters. Each character can either be a lowercase letter (a-f) or a digit (0-5). How many passwords can be generated if each password must contain exactly 5 lowercase letters and 3 digits? (b) Without repetition.
blocks.explanation:
Same three jobs as part (a), but now the 5 letters are all different and the 3 digits are all different.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{5} \times {}^{6}P_{5} \times {}^{6}P_{3}\).
steps:
Given: as in part (a), but no letter and no digit may repeat.
To find: the number of passwords.
Method: Positions by \({}^{8}C_{5}\); ordered letters without repetition \({}^{6}P_{5}\); ordered digits without repetition \({}^{6}P_{3}\).

Choose the letter positions
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = 56\]
Why: Exactly as in part (a).

Fill the positions
\[{}^{6}P_{5} = 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 = 720\]
\[{}^{6}P_{3} = 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 = 120\]
Why: The first letter position has 6 choices, the next 5, and so on; the same for digits.

Multiply
\[720 \times 120 = 86400\]
\[56 \times 86400 = 4838400\]
Why: The three jobs are done together.

Check
\[86400 \times 56 = 86400 \times 50 + 86400 \times 6\]
\[= 4320000 + 518400 = 4838400 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Splitting 56 gives the same product; it is smaller than part (a), as it must be.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints (i) 86,400 and (ii) 120. 86,400 \(= {}^{6}P_{5} \times {}^{6}P_{3}\) is the no-repetition count with letters and digits in fixed positions: it misses the \({}^{8}C_{5} = 56\) ways of placing the letters, and it is listed under 'with repetition'. 120 fits neither part. Correct: (a) 94,058,496; (b) 4,838,400.
